summary.headline: Tata Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY in constant currency to US$178M; operating EBITDA margin held at 16.1% despite salary increments.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed constant-currency revenue growth of 22.2% YoY to US$178M, with services up 26.2% YoY (22.1% excluding ES-Tec). Total revenue in INR rose 2.1% QoQ to INR 1,699 crore, held back by a Technology Solutions decline tied to a revenue-recognition change and education timing. Operating EBITDA margin was 16.1%, flat QoQ, absorbing a ~100bp salary-increment headwind, and PAT was INR 171 crore. Management reiterated strong double-digit FY27 growth and said margins should expand in H2, while ES-Tec (Germany) remains soft.

segments.name: Automotive (ex ES-Tec)
segments.commentary: Grew 7.6% QoQ in USD; about 16% YoY per CFO. Automotive remains the primary growth engine.

segments.name: Non-automotive
segments.commentary: Grew 7.5% QoQ in USD, in line with automotive on a QoQ basis.

segments.name: ES-Tec (Germany)
segments.commentary: Demand subdued, especially from its largest German customer; additional softness expected in Q3, with stabilisation guided for 2027.

segments.name: Technology Solutions (product and education)
segments.commentary: INR 343 crore, +9.2% YoY cc but -6.6% QoQ, due to education revenue timing and Ind AS 115 change on OEM-hosted SaaS licences (reduced revenue by INR 12.6 crore from 1 July 2026). Product business expected to recover in Q3; education faces near-term pressure from customer site infrastructure readiness.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Described as an emerging second growth engine; focus on manufacturing engineering, propulsion, MRO, digital and AI; Airbus relationship cited as foundation. No revenue figure disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated strong double-digit consolidated revenue growth for FY27.
Expects sequential margin improvement in H2 FY27; management said margins expand in Q3 despite typically soft Q3.
Management reaffirmed 18% and 20% as the North Star margin range; no date given for reaching 18%.
Expects some additional softness at ES-Tec in Q3, with conditions to stabilise in 2027.
Expects product business to recover in Q3 on seasonal demand; education to face near-term pressure.
Expects new large programmes, including the US$138M deal, to contribute more meaningfully in H2 FY27 and inform order book for next year and the year after.
Expects to win a couple of further large deals before calendar year-end and continuing into Q4.
capex_capacity: Invested in a new office facility in Pune to consolidate operations and add capacity; this raised D&A and lease-related interest costs.
Added ~300 associates in Q2 for strategic programme ramp-ups; headcount 12,895.
Nearly 1,000 associates are developing and deploying AI agents across engineering and business processes.
Subcontracting rose in Q2 as programmes ramped; management expects it to fall as permanent headcount scales, while retaining flexibility for peaks and troughs.
Learning: over 27,000 learning hours delivered and 5,000+ associates trained in Q2; AI readiness enablement covered over 1,000 employees.
demand_pricing: Five large deals secured in Q2, including a US$138M full vehicle engineering programme with a luxury European OEM spanning two vehicle programmes, running about 2.5 years, with variant opportunities expected.
A North American commercial vehicle maker engaged Tata Technologies to lead end-to-end development of a new platform and digital SDV infrastructure.
Competition: European ESPs in China, Europe and North America; Indian ESPs mainly in India-targeted vehicle programmes.
Management expects structural outsourcing by OEMs as Chinese OEMs set new benchmarks in speed and cost.

Management cited a 25,000-26,000 commercial aircraft fleet expected to exceed 40,000, and no new Boeing or Airbus programme in 10 years; Airbus next-generation single-aisle launch cited as an opportunity.

Anchor-customer (Tata Motors group) demand: management expects to participate in Tata Motors' plans, Iveco acquisition and JLR's North America push. Management declined to comment on competitors' views of anchor demand.
A drop in the US$50M+ client bucket was attributed to a tactical change at one anchor customer ahead of a structural change; management expects a rebound in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not expand QoQ despite the expected ramp of a large deal, and what drove the sharp rise in subcontracting and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the ~10bp margin improvement a good outcome given the salary increments and said attrition fell as a result. Subcontracting is a deliberate balance to cover peaks and troughs in programme execution; it should fall as permanent headcount scales.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aerospace business more predictable and does it stabilise revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Most aerospace programmes run 8-10 years. Management cited 25,000-26,000 commercial aircraft in use scaling to over 40,000, no new Boeing or Airbus programme in 10 years, and an Airbus next-generation single-aisle launch as an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Is Germany weakness worse than expected for 2H, and what changed quarter on quarter at the client level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was delivered as guided and the market played out as anticipated. It cited VW's plan to cut 100,000 jobs by 2030 and a BMW voluntary scheme, expected headwinds for 12-18 months at ES-Tec, and said this does not temper FY27 double-digit growth or 2H margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the drop in the US$50M+ client bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to a tactical change at one anchor customer ahead of a planned structural change within that business. Management expects a rebound in H2 and said it was planned and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline like in auto and non-auto, and how many more large deals are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline is scaling, with large deals increasingly from traditional OEMs following a Japanese OEM programme. Management expects a couple of wins to be shared before calendar year-end, continuing into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US$138M deal net new or renewal, what is its tenure, and who are the competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Some pre-work was done with the customer, and the deal runs about 2.5 years with variant opportunities expected. Competition outside India is mainly European ESPs; Indian ESPs compete mainly on India-targeted vehicle programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Will ES-Tec bounce back from 2027, and what is the auto ex-ES-Tec YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ES-Tec headwinds to ease as the new calendar year begins, with growth from traditional business and the integrated proposition. CFO said automotive excluding ES-Tec grew about 16% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Are we exposed to anchor-customer slowdown, and is 18% margin still achievable by Q4 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on competitors' views but was bullish on Tata Motors group demand, including the Iveco acquisition and JLR's North America push. On margins, 18% and 20% remain the North Star; no date was given for 18%.

risks_watch: ES-Tec (Germany) softness: additional decline expected in Q3, with stabilisation guided only for 2027; largest German customer under restructuring.
Margin trajectory: Q2 EBITDA margin was flat QoQ at 16.1% after a ~100bp salary-increment hit; management expects Q3 expansion and H2 improvement, but the 18% North Star has no date.
Working capital: total DSO rose to 102 days from 97, with unbilled DSO up to 39 days from 32.
Subcontracting rose in Q2 and its normalisation depends on permanent headcount ramp; watch cost and mix.
Technology Solutions: Ind AS 115 change reduced revenue by INR 12.6 crore from 1 July 2026 and education faces near-term pressure from customer site readiness; product recovery expected in Q3.
Anchor-customer timing: a tactical drop in the US$50M+ bucket is expected to rebound in H2; execution of the US$138M deal ramp and the next large-deal wins are key Q3-Q4 checkpoints.
key_quotes: We remain confident in delivering strong double-digit growth for the full year, supported by strong demand, ongoing program ramp-ups, healthy pipeline conversion, continued investment in talent, and improving retention trends.
We believe the combination of product realization expertise, full vehicle development capability, and AI-native delivery creates a powerful competitive advantage for Tata Technologies.
We see the business and the margins associated with it expanding in Q3, even though traditionally Q3 is a soft quarter, and we expect to finish the year very strongly.
We have positioned 18% and 20% as the North Star for our company.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term thesis (full vehicle, aerospace, AI) and on reiterating strong double-digit FY27 growth and H2 margin expansion. More cautious and deliberately vague on ES-Tec timing, anchor-customer specifics, and the date for reaching 18% margin; declined to comment on competitors and on some segment YoY splits.

adds.what: New office facility in Pune to consolidate operations and add capacity

growth.why: Management reiterated strong double-digit FY27 revenue growth, backed by five large Q2 deals including a US$138M luxury-OEM programme, a couple more large wins expected before calendar year-end, and ~300 associates added for ramp-ups; no specific capacity figures or timing given for the guidance.
